strategy.title: No plan: the held market cannot reach $25,000
strategy.why: The only opening (food-vendor permit compliance packs, $400, Brain-produced, $0 capital, 5 days to cash) sells into a counted market of 40 festivals buying one pack a season. Even if all 40 bought, it brings $16,000, short of the new $25,000 target; at the measured 10-of-40 conversion it brings about $4,000. No agreements are recorded.

alternatives.title: Email all 40 registered festivals now
alternatives.why: Costs nothing and Brain can deliver, but the whole register tops out at $16,000 (about $4,000 at the measured rate), so it cannot carry $25,000.

noPlan.decisiveGap: Market volume: $25,000 at $400 needs 63 sales, but the reachable market is 40 festivals buying once a season, so the ceiling is $16,000 even at 100% conversion (about $4,000 at the measured 10-of-40 rate).
noPlan.resolution: Brain researches and counts further reachable buyers with a published count (other states' mass-gathering permit registers, county event-permit lists, other events needing food-vendor compliance) and a higher-value offer for the same buyers; otherwise the owner lowers the target to what the market supports (about $4,000 at the measured rate, $16,000 at most).

excluded.why: Its whole counted market (40 festivals, one purchase each) brings at most $16,000, below the $25,000 target.

constraints.suggestion: Lower the target to about $4,000 (what the 40-festival register supports at the measured conversion; $16,000 is the absolute ceiling with every buyer agreeing).

review.reasons: Revision is on the current contract (digest ac5e0dda..., $25,000 / 30 days / $0 exposure). NO_PLAN is the right stance and the decisive gap is the one the evidence decides: the only opening's counted market is 40 festivals buying one $400 pack a season (EVIDENCE), so the ceiling is 40 x $400 = $16,000 even at 100% conversion, versus 63 sales ($25,000 / $400 = 62.5) needed; at the opening's own measured 10-of-40 conversion it is about $4,000. Every other link (reach, demand, price, conversion, fulfilment by Brain, $6 cost vs $400 price, 5-day settlement) is established, so this is a true TARGET constraint (all the evidence still cannot fit the target), not missing evidence. Arithmetic recomputed and matches; quantities cite the card's sources; no unknown treated as known; no spend, no cash ledger claimed. Resolution (count further reachable buyers with a published count, or lower the target to what the register supports, $16,000 at most) is sound and consistent with Brain's NOT_VIABLE judgement.
